title: C++ Core Guidelines: Bounds and Lifetime Safety

summary: Separates three mutually supporting properties: objects must be used with valid types, accesses must stay inside their allocated bounds, and references must not outlive the objects they designate. The bounds and lifetime profiles translate these ideas into interface and ownership guidance, including range-carrying views and avoiding potentially invalid pointers.
defensive_use: During parser design review, document extent, ownership, and validity duration together. Identify where array-to-pointer conversion discards bounds and where views may outlive storage. Use the Pro.bounds, Pro.lifetime, and GSL.view sections to reason about these component-boundary contracts.
caveats: Bjarne Stroustrup and Herb Sutter are credited by the source as editors.
These evolving project guidelines are not the normative ISO language standard or an automatic safety guarantee. Their guarantees depend on enforcement and surrounding code.
The document distinguishes bounds-checked GSL span from std::span; do not infer that every span implementation checks bounds.
